meta.title: Nonograms — picture puzzles without ads
meta.description: Fill in cells by the numbers and a picture appears. Every picture is solved by reasoning alone, without guessing; hints are free. Grids of 5×5, 10×10 and 15×15 and a picture of the day. No ads, accounts or tracking; works offline.

game.tip: The numbers tell how many cells in a row are filled, in order. Tap a cell to fill it; run your finger along a line to fill several.
game.tipZoom: The grid is zoomed in: move and zoom it with two fingers, or drag a strip of numbers. “Whole picture” shows all of it.
game.fullWrong: As many cells are filled as the numbers ask, but there is a mistake somewhere. “Hint” shows where.

about.title: About the game
about.rules: The numbers beside a row and above a column are the lengths of its groups of filled cells, in order, with at least one empty cell between groups: “3 1” is three filled cells in a row, then an empty one, then one filled. Fill the cells so every row and column fits its numbers, and a picture appears. A cross is a note for yourself: “empty here”; it does not change the result.
about.text: Every picture is solved by reasoning, line after line, without guessing. Hints are free and without limits. No ads, accounts or tracking: progress stays on this device. Works offline.
about.zoom: Large grids on a phone: move and zoom with two fingers; the strips of numbers can be dragged with one; “Whole picture” shows all of the grid. With a mouse: the wheel moves the grid, Ctrl and the wheel zoom.
about.keys: Keyboard: arrows — move over the cells, Space or Enter — like a tap, X — cross, Backspace — clear, H — hint, Ctrl+Z — undo, F — whole picture, Esc — close.
